title: FOUNDATION MODEL-ORIENTED ROBUSTNESS: ROBUST IMAGE MODEL EVALUATION WITH PRETRAINED MODELS
findings: The paper makes no experimental findings related to religion. In a discussion section on societal bias, it notes that relying on large pre-trained models for supervision could cause the evaluated models to inherit biases present in the foundation models' training data, which might include stereotypes or discrimination related to religion, race, gender, or age.

measurement_description: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. The research focuses on evaluating the robustness of image classification models. It briefly mentions that relying on large foundation models could potentially introduce societal biases, including religious bias, but it does not test for or measure this phenomenon.
